cells.tense: The pattern is visible to you here, and you are reading it from inside.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Take the plan you already completed or the shelf you already built, and put it to work for an hour without adding anything. Let being done be the whole point.
cells.core:
When you stand back far enough to see the shape of something, you can still feel every part of it from the inside. You don't have to choose between taking it apart and leaving it alone. It usually reads to others as if the plan came easily, because the drive and the feeling point the same way for you, and the going feels like rhythm rather than force.

Let a finished thing stand. Not improve it, not explain it, not open the tab with the next idea — just be satisfied with it for an hour. The vision feeding forward is what's available when what you already made is allowed to be done. That's the trade you're not making yet: more building instead of the hour where the built thing is enough.

cells.tense: You are seeing the shape of it now, and the next move is already being written in your head.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Top of a page, one line: what this is actually for. Then close the notebook. No plan after it, no revisions, nothing until you next sit down.
cells.core:
You can stand far enough back to take in the whole thing, and the pull is to close the gap before the recognition has settled. Something still forming gets read for what it might fail to be; what should have a rhythm gets a schedule. You are the least served by that — the direction is loud enough for you and the polish is for someone else.

Gather it into a single line instead. What is this for, said in a sentence you could hear spoken and not wince. The line won't be the plan; it just keeps the plan from being written by the worry. Then wait. You are already ahead of where you'd normally be at this hour, and moving it forward is the way to keep from finding out.

cells.tense: You used to move with this easily here, and now you are describing it from the doorway.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Name three things in your life that only exist because something else ended. Not goals you might set — what the ending left behind that you still use. Three sentences, kept where you'll see them.
cells.core:
At your best in this, you read the shape from inside it, and the direction and the feeling ride together. From where you're standing now, the whole pattern is easier to describe than to use, and the moving itself is part of what you're watching. What you had is real, and it got set down while it was still owed something.

The direction comes back through gathering, not pushing — you are not going to revive it by deciding to want something. Name three things that only exist because something else ended. Not goals you might set — what the ending left behind that you're still using. The reading comes back after the account is made.

cells.tense: You are seeing the whole pattern through, and the credit for the reading sits in another name.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Pick a way you read things — how you handle a person, how you run a job — and note who you first learned it from. Then do it once more today, your name beside theirs.
cells.core:
You read the pattern from outside the system while still in it — that hasn't stopped. What's gone quiet is knowing that the reading is yours. It gets described as instinct, or as nothing, and it keeps arriving in conversations as the combined product of other people. So it doesn't get attended to; it gets covered for.

Deepen it by persisting at it. Choose one place you read — a relationship, the way you run a thing — and keep it for three days running, one honest look a day. The reading is a craft that isn't credited yet. Owning one small one is what returns it, and it comes back once the account is kept in your hand.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest move is claiming the person with Balance is already integrated enough to 'let a finished thing land' — the record says the capacity is present-centered, and my read treats 'works with the pen in hand' as 'has a finished thing.' The reader could reasonably answer that nothing here is finished, so savouring a finished thing is not theirs to do. The ask survives being wrong: 'use the good plan you already made one more time on the thing you already built' teaches something either way. The sentence serving the writer is the one in Too Little using 'excess' — it is an abstraction placed in the person's hands, and it goes; it becomes the concrete photo-taking picture of Too Much and the concrete naming of the past in Too Little, which are the same failure without the adjective.
